# Contributing

Thanks for looking. This is a personal project built in the open: it is a tool its author uses, and
a battle test for the [vukem](https://vukem.dev) framework. Contributions are welcome within that
shape.

## Before you write code

Read [ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md) and take an unchecked task, or open an issue first. Two things are
worth knowing before you start:

- [docs/brainstorming.md](../docs/brainstorming.md) records the decisions and **why**. They are
  final unless that file is updated first. If you disagree with one, argue there — not in a pull
  request that quietly does something else.
- [docs/web-research.md](../docs/web-research.md) records every conversion engine, its exact
  licence and its traps. A new engine needs an entry there, and its licence on the `/licenses`
  page, before the feature that uses it ships.

A pull request that adds a feature the ROADMAP does not list will be read, but expect a
conversation about scope before it is read closely.

## Setting up

Requirements: Go (the version in `go.mod`), [Bun](https://bun.com), Docker for the image, and
PostgreSQL for the schema tests.

```bash
bun install
cp .env.example .env
go run ./cmd/app key:generate
go run ./cmd/app migrate
bun run dev              # Vite
go run ./cmd/app serve   # the app
```

The engines a tool needs (`ffmpeg`, `yt-dlp`, `vips`, `gs`) must be on `PATH` or configured. Tests
that need an absent engine skip, so a green run on a bare machine does not mean the conversion
works — `go run ./cmd/app about` prints which engines were resolved.

## The bar

Every commit holds the gates in [ROADMAP.md](../ROADMAP.md#global-quality-gates):

```bash
go build ./... && go vet ./... && golangci-lint run ./...
go test -race -count=1 ./...
bun run typecheck && bun run build
bun run lint:md
```

The schema tests need a server: `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://... go test ./tests/`. CI always
provides one, so those tests never skip there.

Non-negotiable, because the whole point of this project is the quality bar:

- **Fix the root cause.** No `//nolint`, no skipped test, no silenced error to make a check pass.
- **Test the malicious case**, not only the happy path: wrong magic bytes, oversized input, path
  traversal in a filename, a cancelled job, a timeout.
- **Measure before claiming.** Any performance claim needs `go test -bench . -benchmem` and a row
  in [docs/benchmarks.md](../docs/benchmarks.md). A number without its command is not a benchmark.
- **Stream, never buffer a whole file.** This runs on a small container.
- **Engines run as subprocesses**, with a timeout, a process-group kill and `setrlimit`. No cgo.
  See [`.claude/rules/engines.md`](../.claude/rules/engines.md).
- **Detect types from magic bytes.** Never the extension, never the client's `Content-Type`.
- English everywhere: code, comments, docs and UI. There is no i18n layer.

## Commits and releases

[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/), English, with a scope from
[`.claude/rules/commits.md`](../.claude/rules/commits.md):

```text
feat(pixelsvg): merge adjacent runs into maximal rectangles

Refs: S2.1
```

`commitlint` runs in the `commit-msg` hook and in CI. Never `--no-verify`.

`CHANGELOG.md` is generated by [git-cliff](https://git-cliff.org) from those messages, so a bad
commit message becomes a bad release note. Do not hand-edit the changelog; write the message well.

Versions follow [SemVer](https://semver.org) and the changelog follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/). Version tags are pushed one at a time —
GitHub creates no push event for more than three tags in a single push, so the release workflow
would silently never run.

## Agents

This repository is set up for agent-assisted development: [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and
`.claude/` hold the rules, the skills and the project's own workflows. If you use an agent, it is
still your pull request: you are expected to have read what it wrote and to be able to defend it.

## Licensing

The project is MIT. By contributing you agree your work is released under it.

Several conversion engines are GPL or AGPL and run as separate processes; that is why the site
declares no commercial use. Do not add a dependency whose licence is incompatible with that, and do
not copy code out of a GPL project into this one — the Pixels to SVG tool was reimplemented from
published algorithms for exactly this reason.
